status: pre-registered in one commit with the control and the scorer, before the change to LIA and before any SIG-83 run or score; not to be edited after the first run
hypothesis: n/a (build, apparatus for H2). LIA's detection gains a category-independent path: a regular repayment to a listed lender is detected whatever its Enrich category. Results are reported as run.

rulings.SIG-83 description: Colin, 27 November 2026: fix LIA's detection before SIG-76's expected states; don't re-select scenario B
rulings.40766: Colin, 27 November 2026, on 40754: lender names from LENDER_NAMES 1.2.0 only (no alias table); the ROT13 negative control as proposed; matching, recurrence, exclusions and scorer as written in 40754; this pre-registration committed before any run

versions.detector_before: 1.0.0 (SIG-18), unchanged and still what SIG-18's and SIG-57's code calls
versions.detector_after: 1.1.0: 1.0.0's steps (a) to (c) unchanged, plus step (d) below, run only when LIA asks for it

rule.where: step (d) of the detector, after 1.0.0's steps (a) to (c), on the same window feed LIA already passes it (the GR-3 gate applied, LIA's lookback)
candidates: a debit (amount below 0) in a transaction and savings account, dated on or before the as-of date
whose narrative, or failing that whose biller name, names a lender on LENDER_NAMES 1.2.0, whatever its Enrich category

naming is as LIA's display matching (lenders.ts) names a listed lender: the longest listed name the text's words start with, tried as written, then with the product words skipped, then with the product and sensitive words skipped; a word of digits only is dropped first
the biller name is read the same way, and only when the narrative names no listed lender
excluded: a debit whose narrative has a BSB and account number (the detector's own-account rule, BSB_NUMBER)
a debit categorised transfer (this covers card repayments already typed as transfers)
a debit 1.0.0's step (b) already reads as a lender outflow (a liability category, or a biller naming a credit card); it stays with 1.0.0
rule.family: credit_card when the narrative or biller name has the word CARD, else loan
rule.provider: the listed lender name, as listed
rule.grouping: candidates are grouped by family and listed lender name
recurrence: the group's median amount is taken over all its debits; a debit is near when within 5% of that median

sorted by date (then transaction ID), every interval between consecutive near debits is in one and the same band: weekly, 4 to 10 days (7 ± 3); fortnightly, 11 to 17 days (14 ± 3); or monthly, within 3 days of the same day of the next calendar month (clamped to the month's last day)
rule.output: a group that recurs is a liability with source outflow, its cadence, occurrences, median amount and monthly amount (weekly × 52/12, fortnightly × 26/12, monthly × 1) and its near debits as evidence, exactly as 1.0.0 writes one
rule.no_overlap: a group whose family and lender already have a liability from steps (a) to (c) adds nothing; that liability is unchanged
rule.declared: as 1.0.0: declared when a declaration of the same family has that provider after normaliseProvider
rule.fixed: these cut-offs are fixed here and are not LIA's configurable min_occurrences or amount_tolerance, which keep their values for steps (a) to (c)

negative_control.what: every listed lender name (LENDER_NAMES 1.2.0, longest first, whole words, case-insensitive) in a debit's narrative and biller name is replaced by its ROT13 (letters shifted 13 places, case kept, digits and everything else unchanged). Amounts, dates, categories, IDs and declarations are unchanged
negative_control.check: after rotation no debit's narrative or biller name names a listed lender by the rule's matching, and no rotated name is itself on LENDER_NAMES; the run stops if either fails
negative_control.run: first, on set v2.2, both arms (1.3.6 and 1.4.0) on the rotated feed
negative_control.passes_if: on the rotated v2.2, 1.4.0's recall from non-liability categories is no higher than 1.3.6's, and 1.4.0's precision is no lower than 1.3.6's
negative_control.if_it_fails: stop and report; no other result stands

scorer.basis: SIG-57's scorer (src/research/sig57/score.ts): undisclosed liabilities against ground truth, matched one-to-one by family and identity; precision = true positives / found undisclosed, recall = true positives / undisclosed truth. Truth types map to families by SIG-57's TYPE_FAMILY; applicants with at least 3 months of history
scorer.identity: for scoring only, a found provider and a truth provider are resolved to an identity through SIG-57's alias table 1.0.0, in both arms alike, as SIG-57 scored. The rule never reads the table (40766, 1)
scorer.found: LIA's liabilities (assessLia), not the bare detector, with the detector's declared flag, so both arms are LIA as the composition runs it
scorer.recall_from_non_liability_categories: true positives whose evidence has no debit in a liability category (loan_repayment, bnpl, sacc_loan, wage_advance), over undisclosed truth
scorer.also_reported: by family; the liabilities found by step (d); false-positive causes as SIG-57 names them (FP1 declared not matched, FP2 not a liability, FP3 duplicate)
scorer.categories: the pinned Enrich build (1.8.0, moroku-enrich 8cdb0d9, taxonomy 1.4): set v1 from research/enrich/synthetic-v1-categories-engine-1.8.0.json; set v2.2 from research/enrich/synthetic-v2.2-categories-no-biller-code-engine-1.8.0.json (no biller codes, SIG-57 A1); set v2.3 categorised at run time on the pinned build with biller codes, as SIG-81 and the demo do

runs_in_order: 1. negative control, set v2.2 rotated, arms 1.3.6 and 1.4.0
2. set v2.2, the scoring set, arms 1.3.6 and 1.4.0
4. set v2.3, the demo set, arms 1.3.6 and 1.4.0; reported, never used to choose anything
records: research/runs/sig83-<run>.json, one per run, through scripts/lib/run-record.js; IDs, families, identities and counts only, never a narrative

from_the_ticket: no fall in precision or recall against LIA 1.3.6 on set v2.2
a gain in recall from debits in non-liability categories that repay a lender
set v1 stays at 1.00 and 1.00, and 1.4.0's liabilities on v1 are byte-identical to 1.3.6's
fails_if: precision on set v2.2 falls below LIA 1.3.6's
the rule was changed after a score on set v2.2 or v2.3 was seen

scenario_b: set v2.3's syn-v23-9bd03ecbd72ba13e: recorded as computed. Its narrative names COMMBANK, which isn't on LENDER_NAMES 1.2.0, so under this rule it is expected not to be a candidate; whatever the run gives is recorded, and nothing is tuned for it
